answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a refundable bond tied to one verified identity record, like a crystal entry in a shared ledger that cannot be duplicated cheaply. To forge a new identity, an attacker must lock fresh funds and slowly earn trust through attested work, so mass-producing fake agents becomes expensive. Honest agents keep a steady pulse of completed, peer-verified transactions, while sudden newcomers with no history are rate-limited until they prove themselves.
